title: HSBC Global Economic Seminar (slides): Weak Growth, Volatile-Driven Inflation, Two-Sided Risks
source: bcch (apresentação em PDF colada pelo analista; só slides)
summary: Naudon's HSBC deck is organised around weak growth, above-target inflation and their policy consequences, and the balance tilts toward activity: Q3 GDP fell 1.1% y/y mainly on mining, non-mining growth is weak, domestic demand has been weaker than expected and investment fell 6.7% y/y. Inflation is framed as heavily driven by volatile prices, with headline at 4.5% but ex-volatiles core at 3.3%, an implicit look-through argument, although the charts also show 11-month expectations drifting up. He spends a third of the deck on the external side, attributing the near-zero real-rate differential with the US to different cycles and higher US term premia, and arguing that it has weighed on the real exchange rate but is not the whole story. On policy he only shows the September IPoM corridor with 'risks in both directions', with no explicit path. This is his first speech in the base; it reads as a balanced hold, softer than Céspedes (17/11) and clearly softer than the October minutes, where a 25bp hike was on the table, although the slides-only format limits the read.
